solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reductions in spending involving mostly substantial measures

indicators.note: the spending cuts wrap themselves around the other piece, taking it in

parts.note: budget reductions are cuts

indicators.note: most of the word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: substantial means big

explanation.surface: A report on austerity: budget cuts that include some fairly hefty measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient unit of length, roughly forearm length, so cubits are measures.

clue.text: Transport old woman to European city of old

parts.note: a cart is a means of transport
a hag is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: Taking an old lady by cart to an ancient European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the ancient North African city destroyed by Rome, a city of antiquity.

clue.text: Leader of band gives help to musicians

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of band

parts.note: to give help is to assist, so assists

explanation.surface: A bandleader lending a hand to the players.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassists play the bass guitar or double bass, so they are musicians.

clue.text: Aspirin finally taken during commotion, bringing relief

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the fuss, so inside it

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of Aspirin

explanation.surface: Taking an aspirin in the middle of a fuss brings relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' is not pain relief: a tondo is a circular carved relief or painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tondo is a round sculpted relief or circular painting, so a kind of relief.

clue.text: There are two types of Conservative, Balls and Miliband admitted

parts.note: Conservative can be shortened two ways, CON and C
the second short form of Conservative is the single letter C
Ed Balls, the Labour politician
Ed Miliband, then the Labour leader

explanation.surface: A political sketch: two kinds of Tory, plus two Labour Eds, all owning up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls and Ed Miliband were leading UK Labour politicians in 2013, so each supplies ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede a point is to admit it is true, so conceded is a synonym of admitted.

clue.text: Ham served to Maria well-cooked

indicators.note: cooking the letters thoroughly mixes them into a new order

explanation.surface: A dish of ham given to Maria, cooked through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like the meat on the plate, but it is the verb to overact.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham it up is to overact, the same as making something too theatrical.

clue.text: Actor not perturbed about beginning to lose voice

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit around the other piece
perturbed means disturbed, so the letters are shaken up
the beginning of lose is its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor, calm about starting to lose his voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perturbed' rearranges ACTORNOT into CONTRATO, and 'about' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Contralto is the lowest female singing voice, so a voice type.

clue.text: Woman expected to take girl about?

definitions.text: Woman expected to take girl about?

parts.note: something expected is due

indicators.note: the girl's name is read the other way round

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman who is supposed to escort a girl around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' joins the pieces; the question mark admits the whole clue is only loosely the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone to a young girl, escorting her about.

clue.text: After start of demolition, a building is completely destroyed

indicators.note: the start of demolition is its opening letter

parts.note: a shed is a small building

explanation.surface: A building wrecked once demolition gets under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes dashed are shattered, so dashed means utterly destroyed.

clue.text: Sticky stuff on back of walls at home

parts.note: RE means on, as in regarding

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, taken from walls

parts.note: someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Something tacky smeared on the rear of the walls at home.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the crossword's 'on', in the sense 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a viscous gum oozing from trees, a classic sticky substance.

clue.text: Innocence of English family touring loch

indicators.note: the family goes round the English letter, so that letter sits inside

parts.note: a clan is a family group
Loch Ness, the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: An innocent English family on a holiday tour round a Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleanness in the moral sense is purity or freedom from guilt, a synonym of innocence.

clue.text: Chases soldier around in part of China

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a soldier about in a region of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but here it is china, crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole dish is an item of crockery, one piece in a china set.

clue.text: Hateful fellow inside house, demolishing its walls

parts.note: a fellow is a he
inside means in

indicators.note: knocking down the walls of the word house leaves only its middle letters

explanation.surface: A nasty man inside a house, knocking down its walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolishing its walls' strips the outer H and E of house, leaving OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous describes something utterly wicked and odious, hence hateful.

clue.text: Upset and possibly angered (or enraged)

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of angered might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone upset, maybe angry, or even enraged.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'or enraged' is a second fodder: ENRAGED is also an anagram of the same seven letters, so either word works with 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to upset or throw into disorder, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fail to visit great Chinese landmark

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a business collapsing or going bust
literally travelling to the Great Wall of China

explanation.surface: A traveller who fails to make the trip to the Great Wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to collapse or be ruined; read literally it is a trip to the Great Wall.

clue.text: Boss has little time at work: out to lunch for the most part

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
OP is operating, in operation or at work

indicators.note: most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: someone out to lunch is crazy, bananas

explanation.surface: A boss who has hardly any time at the office because he is out at lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' means crazy here, not having a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal for the person in charge, the leader or boss.

clue.text: Column, one with protective clothing all around

indicators.note: the covering surrounds the other letter completely

parts.note: a plaster covers and protects a wound
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pillar, and someone wrapped in protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a rectangular column set into a wall.

clue.text: Writer from East End, half-forgotten

indicators.note: the writer's name is taken out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A half-forgotten author from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across eaST END HALf. The East End is a working-class area of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stendhal was the French novelist who wrote The Red and the Black.

clue.text: Champion racing driver going round track on island

indicators.note: the driver's name encircles the other pieces

parts.note: Alain Prost, the French Formula One champion
to track someone is to tag along after them

explanation.surface: A champion Formula One driver lapping a circuit on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' looks like it describes the driver, but it is the definition: a supporter of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist is a leading advocate of a cause, so a champion of it.

clue.text: Shout "Riot"

definitions.meaning: informally, a hilariously funny person or thing

explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud cry, and also slang for something hilarious, just like a riot.

clue.text: Top athlete?

definitions.meaning: a garment for the upper body, such as a sweater
a sportsman who competes in leaping events

explanation.definitionFit: A jumper is a knitted sweater worn on top, and also an athlete who leaps.

clue.text: Daring of us to enter place of confinement

indicators.note: the possessive goes into the cage, so it sits inside

parts.note: a cage confines animals
belonging to us is ours, our

explanation.surface: A bold act of ours, going into a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage is bravery, the quality of being daring.

clue.text: Shy child with guardian getting round in pub

indicators.note: the turned piece goes in the pub, inside its letters

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: turning round reads the word for the child backwards

parts.note: a ward is a child under a guardian

explanation.surface: A shy youngster taken into a pub by a guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: Indrawn means withdrawn or reserved in manner, so shy.

clue.text: Wife's responsibility, mostly to children

definitions.note: the 's stands for has, linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: most of the word, its final letter cut off

parts.note: a duty is a responsibility

explanation.surface: A wife's role, largely to look after the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch is Cockney slang for a wife, from 'duchess', as in 'my old Dutch'.

clue.text: Stress English politician suffers, having pay increase initially declined

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
to suffer an illness is to have it, as in he has flu

indicators.note: the first letter has been turned down, so removed

parts.note: a pay increase in Britain is a rise

explanation.surface: An English MP under stress after a pay rise was refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially declined' drops the R of RISE, leaving ISE. A RISE is the British word for a pay raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Little one starts to tremble if teacher chastises him

indicators.note: the starting letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A small pupil who shakes when the teacher tells him off.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is informal British for a tiny person, especially a small child.

clue.text: Chairman endlessly distracted by one type of music

indicators.note: a distracted mind is in disorder, so the letters are jumbled
without its end, the last letter of Chairman goes

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A chairman put off his stride by some kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts N from Chairman; 'distracted' rearranges CHAIRMA into MARIACH, then I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariachi is a style of Mexican folk music played by strolling bands.

clue.text: Woman becoming involved in debauchery lately

indicators.note: the name is caught up within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A woman who has recently been drawn into debauchery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheryl is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a woman.
